name: Coordination and Reporting
one_liner: Translate the team's rituals and metrics for everyone outside the agile team.
purpose: Agile practices have developed specific terms, rituals, formats and metrics, but an Agile Project Core Team does not work in isolation: other non-agile teams and stakeholder groups have their own informational needs and preferences. PM²-Agile addresses this by adjusting the types of information, formats, granularity, language and frequency of communication. Internally the team coordinates face to face through its ceremonies; externally it coordinates through regular project meetings and reports.
meta: External coordination with other layers; internal coordination inside the A-PCT
Development Status Report — TeCo responsible, PM accountable

diagram.sec: Three groups of reporting and planning units
items: Delivery units — e.g. work packages, deliveries
Functional units — e.g. use cases, business processes, capabilities, features
Work units — e.g. work items like user stories, enabler stories, bugs
Link them: stories group into a feature; features link to a delivery unit

diagram.sec: Five themes coordinated with other groups
items: Planning — a Release Plan that integrates with the overall project work plan
Reporting — progress metrics and frequency aligned with other teams' accepted metrics
Architecture — artefacts following organisation standards so analysis costs no overhead
Deployment and Transition — PCT and A-PCT working with the IT operations team
Risk — technical and project risks following the PM² Risk Management Process and Risk Log

fields.what: There may be other non-agile teams in the project plus stakeholder groups with specific informational needs and preferences.
fields.pollux: The portal team must report alongside ESM units that never went agile.

fields.what: PM²-Agile adjusts the types of information, formats, granularity, language and frequency of communication to those needs.
fields.pollux: Lovelace reformats burndown data into something Gantt's office accepts.

fields.what: The A-PCT provides a Release Plan that is easy to understand and integrates with the overall project work plan.
fields.pollux: Four release dates sit inside the eighteen-month project timeline.

fields.what: The A-PCT's progress metrics and reporting frequency should align with the metrics accepted by other teams and management layers.
fields.pollux: Iteration metrics roll into the Project Status Report you own.

fields.what: Architecture artefacts follow organisation standards so impact assessment, reusability and interoperability analysis need no extra overhead.
fields.pollux: Einstein documents to ESM enterprise architecture conventions.

fields.what: The PCT and A-PCT work with the IT operations team; transparency enables collaboration supporting processes such as software configuration management.
fields.pollux: Operations join early for the transition into service on 31 Jan 2030.

fields.what: A-PCTs may capture both technical and other project risks following the PM² Risk Management Process and using artefacts such as the Risk Log.
fields.pollux: The risk that Babbage's engine is never finished goes in the Risk Log.

fields.what: The coarsest planning and reporting group — for example work packages and deliveries.
fields.pollux: Each of the four POLLUX releases reports as a delivery.

fields.what: The middle group — use cases, business processes, capabilities and features.
fields.pollux: 'Reconciliation panel' is a feature reported at this level.

fields.what: The finest group — work items such as user stories, enabler stories and bugs.
fields.pollux: The stories Curie prioritises in the Work Items List.

fields.what: Wherever possible link the units: stories group into a feature, and features link to a specific delivery unit.
fields.pollux: Every story traces up to a release, so progress is visible to Medici.

fields.what: Linking the units allows more effective external coordination by giving stakeholders a clear view of execution and delivery.
fields.pollux: Answers 'what will Release 3 contain' without opening the team's board.

fields.what: External coordination is facilitated through project follow-up meetings, Project Status Reports, and demos and deliverables acceptance events.
fields.pollux: Demos to national authorities become acceptance events for Release 3.

fields.what: Internal coordination within an A-PCT is supported by open, frequent, efficient and face-to-face communication.
fields.pollux: Daily Stand-up every morning, review and retrospective each fortnight.

fields.what: Daily Stand-up, Iteration Planning, Iteration Review and Iteration Retrospective carry the team's internal communication.
fields.pollux: Conflict 4 — the stand-up must not become the PM's status meeting.

traps: The three groups are delivery units, functional units and work units — in that order.
Stories group into features; features link to a delivery unit, never the reverse.
A-PCT risks still follow the PM² Risk Management Process and its Risk Log.
Internal coordination is face-to-face; external coordination runs on meetings and reports.
The Development Status Report is the TeCo's, not the Product Owner's.
